answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable cost: a small stake locked behind a unique hardware-backed attestation, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Like an ember that only stays lit while it is fed, a velvet-smooth onboarding flow should still demand proof of ongoing useful work before reputation accrues. Identities left idle in the tundra of unused accounts, never attesting or completing tasks, should decay and lose privileges, so real agents earn trust through sustained contribution while cheap copies fade away.
